nodes.label: Cosine similarity diversity measure
nodes.rationale: Catches directional similarity between the weak learners' feature vectors; paired with Pearson because the two are complementary.

nodes.label: Similarity-matrix diversity loss
nodes.rationale: Build an nxn similarity matrix over the MLPs' output feature vectors and penalise the mean off-diagonal, so the MLPs cannot all learn the same thing; more diversity was expected to mean more accuracy.

nodes.label: Diversity-weight ablation (sweet spot 0.05)
nodes.rationale: val_loss 0.2855 (w=0) → 0.2814 (w=0.05) → 0.3028/0.3058/0.3035 at 0.10/0.50/1.00. Negative final div values mean the optimizer pushed the MLPs past 'different' into anti-correlated, spending capacity on being opposite rather than useful — so diversity must act as a regularizer, not the primary objective.

nodes.label: Diversity-weight scheduling (warm-up vs annealing)
nodes.rationale: Warm-up (div_w = min(target, target*epoch/warmup_epochs)) is preferred over annealing because applying diversity pressure before the MLPs have learned anything leaves nothing useful to diversify — mirroring boosting, where diversity is a consequence of the sequential structure rather than forced from the start. Turns the ablation into a 2D grid of target weight x schedule type.

nodes.label: Pearson correlation diversity measure
nodes.rationale: Catches linear redundancy in what the MLPs learned, which cosine similarity alone misses; `combined` mode averages both.

nodes.label: detach_mean (stop-gradient ensemble mean)
nodes.rationale: Proven analytically and in ncl.py's self-test not to matter under this codebase: training.py does ONE joint .backward() over the summed loss of all K learners, so the per-learner detach factor exactly cancels against cross-terms from the other K-1 penalties. Settled before running any experiment.

nodes.label: Feature bagging
nodes.rationale: Each expert sees a random ~70% column subset. Chosen as v4's only diversity mechanism because it needs no artificial diversity penalty (which V1 required and v4 showed to be unnecessary). Subsets are HARD and frozen at construction, which is also its limitation (motivates feature gating).

nodes.label: Negative Correlation Learning (ncl.py)
nodes.rationale: Per-learner penalty rewarding deviation from the ensemble mean, added because nothing in the LOSS previously pushed learners to disagree. Best λ=1.0 beat our XGBoost and published FT-Transformer on California Housing (0.4039), but generalization is mixed (1 of 3 in notebook 12) and the -λ(F_i-F̄)² term is unbounded below, which on BCE-with-logits collapses the classifier to a constant class at λ≥0.2.

nodes.label: λ>1 NCL breakdown boundary
nodes.rationale: ncl.py's toy self-test (K=6 linear heads on half the features each) showed ensemble MSE falling 3.74→0.097 as λ went 0→1.0 then breaking down sharply past λ≈1.0; real data reproduced it (λ=1.5 → RMSE 1.03 vs 0.40). The literature's λ∈[0,1] guidance was re-derived empirically rather than taken from memory, and the failure was found before any real experiment.

nodes.label: V1 quirk: lambda_div multiplied by 0.0
nodes.rationale: V1's CKA diversity term never actually affects the loss — so V1's reported numbers were never produced by the diversity penalty it claims, which is part of why v4 concluded the penalty was unnecessary.

nodes.label: V1 quirk: resample_feature_subsets() is a no-op
nodes.norm_label: v1 quirk: resample_feature_subsets() is a no-op
nodes.rationale: Subsets are re-drawn with the same fixed seed every epoch, so the 'resampled' subsets are identical — V1's subsets were effectively fixed, the behaviour v4 adopted deliberately.

nodes.label: Original SRP design brief (weak-learner MLPs → attention)
nodes.norm_label: original srp design brief (weak-learner mlps → attention)
nodes.rationale: MLPs deliberately kept to 1-2 layers and 4-16 neurons with weight penalties so each focuses on a few important features; the whole stack is trained end to end and the attention module produces the prediction. Must eventually be validated on large datasets, with small ones (wine, housing) only for visualising the idea.

nodes.rationale: v1 resampled subsets every epoch, which quietly changes what each expert 'means' over time and makes per-expert diagnostics uninterpretable; v4 draws them once from a seed and keeps them for the model's lifetime.

nodes.label: SRP — Sequential Residual Predictor
nodes.rationale: Ensemble of small weak-learner MLPs emits a sequence of feature tokens that a causal transformer block combines into a prediction — chosen to be an end-to-end differentiable analogue of gradient-boosted trees (weak learners + sequential refinement) in PyTorch.

nodes.label: Embedding mode `linear`
nodes.rationale: Per-feature Linear→ReLU, included specifically to test whether merely SEPARATING features (without periodicity) is what helps.

nodes.label: Grinsztajn perturbation diagnostics (noise / rotation / label smoothing)
nodes.norm_label: grinsztajn perturbation diagnostics (noise / rotation / label smoothing)
nodes.rationale: Three published tests reused instead of inventing new ones, so the 'why do trees still win' question is answered against an established protocol.

nodes.label: Two-phase Optuna tuning protocol
nodes.rationale: 24-trial parallel search on a small epoch budget against validation loss, then the winner re-trained on 3 fresh seeds at the full budget and reported on test — the cheap question asked before building anything architectural. It also independently rediscovered that PLR helps (15/24 trials picked periodic), cross-validating Steps 5/7 by a different process.

nodes.label: Piecewise-linear embeddings (PLE)
nodes.rationale: Fixed training-data quantile bin edges, v_t(x)=clip((x-edge[t])/(edge[t+1]-edge[t]),0,1) — no learned frequencies. Built to answer whether PLR's win is about periodicity or just per-feature nonlinearity; it regressed on YearPredictionMSD almost as much as periodic, so the answer was neither. Kept available but not made the default.

nodes.label: PLR embeddings (Periodic → Linear → ReLU)
nodes.rationale: Each feature gets its own private learned frequencies and weights, which is what breaks rotation-invariance (after a rotation the weights no longer line up with the feature). Periodic waves specifically target trees' advantage on irregular/threshold-like functions: a learned high-frequency sine can swing sharply around one feature value. Verified by embeddings.py's own tests (feature-independence, rotation sensitivity, ~10x sharper response than linear) rather than assumed.

nodes.label: Rotation-invariance diagnosis
nodes.rationale: Rotating inputs cost trees up to 17 accuracy points and cost v4 essentially nothing — damning rather than harmless, because it means the model cannot learn 'if income > 50k then...'. This single diagnostic pinpointed per-feature embeddings as the next fix.

nodes.label: V1 quirk: metrics as mean of per-batch metrics
nodes.norm_label: v1 quirk: metrics as mean of per-batch metrics
nodes.rationale: Averaging per-batch RMSE is not the true RMSE, so the v4 benchmark notebook recomputes every metric on the full split — otherwise the V1-vs-v4 comparison would be measuring two different quantities.

nodes.label: One fixed, never-per-dataset-tuned config
nodes.rationale: Every v4 number outside notebook 09 uses notebook 06's single config designed on housing, while every published comparison number is tuned per dataset — stated as a handicap that makes the wins stronger and the losses ambiguous, and named the top remaining lever.

nodes.label: Standardized-target RMSE rescaling correction
nodes.rationale: benchmarks.py/benchmarks_rtdl.py standardise regression targets, so run_config's RMSE must be rescaled by y_std (notebook 08's score_from_raw convention) before comparison. Direction of 'beats baseline' claims was scale-invariant and stayed correct, but a 'beats XGBoost' claim for Facebook Comments was an artifact and was corrected; the rescaling is now built into the notebooks.

nodes.label: CLS-token removal alternatives (mean pool / last token / weighted sum)
nodes.norm_label: cls-token removal alternatives (mean pool / last token / weighted sum)
nodes.rationale: Supervisor asked to drop the CLS token. Last-token read-out was argued most theoretically motivated because under causal attention token K has already attended to everything before it, mirroring boosting's last tree having the most context; mean pooling is simplest and treats all MLPs equally; weighted sum adds K learned softmaxed weights.

nodes.label: [CLS] token aggregation
nodes.rationale: A learnable token appended last so that under the triu causal mask its row is all-zeros and it attends to every weak learner, making it the natural read-out point.

nodes.label: Causal attention aggregator
nodes.rationale: Masked self-attention where expert i sees only experts 1..i, motivated by the boosting analogy of later experts building on earlier ones. Never clearly beat mean-pool; Step 12 showed the ordering is arbitrary (experts are trained jointly, not on frozen residuals) and both attention arms overfit to their fixed learner order.

nodes.label: Causal-order permutation test (notebook 14)
nodes.rationale: Trained models are re-evaluated with the K tokens shuffled — no retraining, same weights, only slot assignment changes. Mean-pool's shuffled variance (0.004) matching pure seed noise is the built-in check that the measurement is trustworthy before trusting what it says about attention. Both attention arms degrade 10-16x more, so the learned slot structure is overfitting to an assignment that was never meaningful.

nodes.label: Mean-pool aggregator
nodes.rationale: Simple average of the K experts; deliberately the control arm everything else must beat, and provably order-invariant so it doubles as the sanity-check reference in permutation tests.

nodes.label: PMA / set-attention aggregator (proposed)
nodes.rationale: A learned query cross-attending over the K expert embeddings as an unordered set — keeps attention in the architecture without the unjustified causal ordering that Step 12 showed to be the source of the attention arms' overfitting. Not yet built.

nodes.label: pool_level="output" (predict-then-average)
nodes.rationale: Mean-pool averages EMBEDDINGS then runs one shared head, but NCL needs each learner's own scalar, so model.py gained predict-then-average as a prerequisite. ncl_lambda=0 under it isolates the confound — and it HURTS on its own (0.4501 vs 0.4202), so the penalty has to overcome a real architectural cost to win.

nodes.label: Weak learner / expert
nodes.rationale: One small MLP, K of them (e.g. K=16); kept small so the ensemble, not any single net, carries the capacity.

nodes.label: Causal mask as gradient-boosting analogy
nodes.rationale: Token i attends only to 0..i (torch.triu(..., diagonal=1) filled with -inf) so that whatever the first learner already captured, the second need not relearn — exactly the gradient-boosted-trees intuition the architecture is built on.

nodes.label: Bidirectional attention aggregator
nodes.rationale: Unmasked variant; retained mainly to isolate the causal mask's own contribution (+0.102 vs +0.068 degradation under shuffle) from the shared learned step embedding both arms carry.

nodes.label: PlainMLP floor reference
nodes.rationale: One ordinary MLP with no expert structure — if the ensemble can't beat this, the whole idea isn't earning its complexity.

nodes.norm_label: v1 — predecessors' architecture (bidirectional attention + [cls] + cka diversity penalty)
nodes.rationale: Vendored unchanged in v1/ and kept as a permanent comparison point; v4 beat it on all 3 Step 6 datasets with ~1/10th the parameters (41k-85k vs 416k).

nodes.label: SRP v4 — from-scratch rebuild

nodes.label: Arm (one full configuration under test)
nodes.rationale: Arms are compared side by side under identical training so a difference is attributable to the switched piece, not to the protocol.

nodes.label: Embedding mode `none`
nodes.rationale: Raw features straight into the experts — v4's behaviour through notebook 05, kept as a true no-op control verified by parameter-count/bit-for-bit checks.

nodes.label: Feature gating (adaptive per-learner feature relevancy)
nodes.rationale: Soft learned gate F_t(x)=F_{t-1}(x)+eta*h_t(g_t(x)*x) in 5 modes, from a predecessor research document, because hard feature bagging gives a learner no way to lean harder on its one useful column. Dynamic gates' final layer is zero-initialised so g_t(x) starts constant ≈0.982 = sigmoid(4.0) — static and dynamic start identically and only training separates them. Verdict: every mode's delta is smaller than its own seed noise, and because the 4 gated variants are flat relative to each other there is no partial signal to amplify by tuning init_bias/hidden_dim.

nodes.label: Identical expert init across arms (make_arm forked RNG)
nodes.norm_label: identical expert init across arms (make_arm forked rng)
nodes.rationale: make_arm() builds the weak-learner ensemble first and runs capacity-matching math under a forked RNG, so for a fixed seed every arm starts from bit-identical expert weights — this is what makes per-seed PAIRED comparisons valid, not just averages.

nodes.label: Per-module [PASS]/[FAIL] self-tests
nodes.rationale: Every core module runs its own checks under __main__ (weak_learners, attention, embeddings, feature_gating, model) with no GPU needed, so the environment and code can be verified in seconds before any notebook result is trusted.

nodes.label: Guiding rule: never assume a new idea helps
nodes.norm_label: guiding rule: never assume a new idea helps
nodes.rationale: Build it, run it next to the old version under an identical protocol, let the numbers say yes or no. Written down explicitly so the project's logic can be re-read without re-deriving it from conversation history.

nodes.label: Findings computed from the run, never hand-typed
nodes.norm_label: findings computed from the run, never hand-typed
nodes.rationale: Each notebook's closing Findings section is Python reading study.best_params / a results DataFrame, specifically so a stale or wrong number cannot survive a copy-paste.

nodes.label: backfill_results.py (documented-source backfill)
nodes.rationale: Transcribes README Steps 6-12 into results/ with source="documented" and no fresh compute — 121 entries behind the ranking table, tagged so transcribed numbers can never be mistaken for re-run ones.

nodes.label: Covertype gap (v4's unresolved weak spot)
nodes.rationale: v4 trails every reference including published plain MLP. Tuning recovered only 41% of the gap (0.0203 → 0.0120), feature gating moved it to 0.0112 (within seed noise), and TabR/TabM at ~0.976-0.977 confirm the gap is against the whole modern lineage, not one 2021 baseline — so the fix must be architectural.

nodes.label: report.json-per-run results convention (results.py)
nodes.rationale: TabR-inspired structured on-disk results (save_report/save_checkpoint/load_reports/summarize_ranks/best_per_dataset); adopted because the reference papers' own analysis code is not public but their per-run reports are, making this the one format that travels.

nodes.label: Published-baseline provenance protocol
nodes.rationale: TabR/TabM numbers were fetched from each repo's committed per-run report.json and every report's test-set `support` total checked against our own split sizes (Adult 16,281; Higgs Small 19,610; Covertype 116,203) before being trusted. TabPFN and TabArena were deliberately NOT added: TabPFN's suites don't overlap these exact splits and TabArena uses 8-fold CV with ROC-AUC/log-loss, so adding either without re-deriving the protocol would not be a real comparison — the gap is reported honestly instead.

nodes.label: Chunked GPU evaluation
nodes.rationale: training.py's evaluate()/predict() process val/test in 4096-row batches to avoid CUDA OOM when parallel workers share a GPU; verified numerically identical to single-pass evaluation to 7 decimal places.

nodes.label: SRP_* environment-variable overrides
nodes.rationale: SRP_SUBSAMPLE/TRIALS/TRIAL_EPOCHS/FINAL_EPOCHS/FINAL_SEEDS/JOBS/KEY/ARM let a headless smoke test shrink any notebook to under a minute with no code edits — the numbers are meaningless, every cell running error-free is the point before committing to a 1.5h GPU run.

nodes.label: GPU cluster workflow (edit → sync → run → copy back)
nodes.norm_label: gpu cluster workflow (edit → sync → run → copy back)
nodes.rationale: Shared university cluster with a preinstalled `srp` conda env (base has no PyTorch); GPU chosen by lowest utilization rather than most free memory because the contention is for compute, not space. The person running Claude Code never SSHes to the server on the user's behalf — every server command is run by the user.

nodes.label: Timestamped progress logs under runs/
nodes.rationale: runs/<NN>_progress_<timestamp>.log with a symlink to the latest, never deleted on restart, so a crashed run's partial progress survives even though the notebook's own outputs don't. runs/ is gitignored, disposable scratch — except when a notebook deliberately reads one back (notebook 10 reloading notebook 09's Optuna study instead of re-typing its winning hyperparameters).

nodes.label: sync_to_server.sh safeguards
nodes.rationale: Refuses to run if hostname says you're already on the server, and backs up anything it would overwrite under ../v4_overwritten_<timestamp>/ so a sync can never silently destroy a notebook whose results weren't copied back.

nodes.label: nbconvert --inplace writes once, at the end
nodes.norm_label: nbconvert --inplace writes once, at the end
nodes.rationale: No incremental checkpointing, so Ctrl-C loses the ENTIRE run, and a fresh run overwrites the notebook file itself — hence always copy results back before syncing new code, and detach long runs with nohup/disown.

nodes.label: READY marker file convention
nodes.rationale: A per-dataset-folder sentinel confirming extraction fully succeeded, so a half-extracted archive can't silently produce a wrong-split benchmark run.

nodes.label: Two dataset tiers (diagnostic samples vs exact published splits)
nodes.norm_label: two dataset tiers (diagnostic samples vs exact published splits)
nodes.rationale: datasets.py gives small 10k-row auto-downloaded samples with our own reproducible splits for fast diagnostics; benchmarks.py/benchmarks_rtdl.py give full-scale data with the papers' exact splits so results are directly comparable to published numbers. A READY marker per dataset folder confirms extraction succeeded.

nodes.label: num-embeddings data archive listing (12 dataset folders)
nodes.norm_label: num-embeddings data archive listing (12 dataset folders)
nodes.rationale: Kept as small metadata in place of the ~3.2GB archive: adult, california, churn, covtype, eye, fb-comments, gesture, higgs-small, house, microsoft, otto, santander — each with X_num_{train,val,test}.npy, y_*, idx_*, info.json and a READY marker. Only higgs-small, fb-comments and santander are actually loaded by benchmarks.py.

nodes.label: RTDL/FT-Transformer data archive listing (11 dataset folders)
nodes.norm_label: rtdl/ft-transformer data archive listing (11 dataset folders)
nodes.rationale: adult, aloi, california_housing, covtype, epsilon, helena, higgs_small, jannis, microsoft, yahoo, year — N_{train,val,test}.npy naming (vs the other archive's X_num_*), plus q_* files for the ranking datasets. All five benchmarks_rtdl.py datasets come from this ONE archive so the published comparison table is internally consistent; ALOI/Helena/Epsilon/Yahoo/Microsoft sit here unextracted.

nodes.label: Dataset arrays excluded from git
nodes.rationale: *.npy/*.npz/*.tar are not tracked because the raw archive alone is ~3.2GB and is easy to refetch/regenerate; only small metadata (info.json, published_gorishniy2022.json, archive_listing.txt) is kept so comparisons stay reproducible without the bulk.
